instruction: Permanently redirect all HTTP traffic for shop.example.com to HTTPS, keeping the path and query string.
Permanently redirect example.net to www.example.net over HTTPS including all subpaths.
Permanently redirect www.blog.example to blog.example, stripping the www prefix from every URL.
Temporarily redirect every visitor of shop-v2.example.com to the maintenance page while the site is being upgraded.
Mark the discontinued product page as gone by returning 410 for /products/old-widget.
Permanently rewrite dated blog URLs of the form /blog/2024/05/my-post to /posts/my-post.
Redirect the old pricing page to the new plans page while preserving any query string.
Internally rewrite incoming /v1/... API documentation requests to /stable/... before serving them from disk.
Add a trailing slash to directory URLs on dirsite.example.com so relative links resolve correctly.
Redirect requests for index.html or home.html to the clean root URL.
Strip the .html extension from article URLs so /article/how-to-nginx.html redirects to /article/how-to-nginx.
Send all requests under /forum to the new community portal at community.example.org, preserving the path.
Rewrite the incoming /legacy/... path to /v2/... and then proxy it to the app on 127.0.0.1:8080 without changing the upstream URI.
Return a 503 maintenance page whenever /var/www/site/maintenance.html exists, and serve the site normally otherwise.
Redirect the root URL of multilingual.example.com to the English locale directory.
Remove trailing slashes from all URLs except the root so /about/ and /about are the same canonical URL.
Send old Internet Explorer users detected by their user agent to the lightweight legacy site.
Force every PDF link under /docs/ to the new documentation portal at docs.example.io.
Rewrite pretty portal URLs like /portal/settings to the PHP script they map to and hand them to PHP-FPM.
Redirect three deprecated marketing URLs to their new locations using an nginx map.
